findings.finding: F1: R7 for asks is not moving a source but indexing text Dispatch has never indexed. Every ask write indexes the question alone (createAsk, editAsk, reviews.go, docs/ask_blocks.go, docs/approval_ask.go, docs/decided_wording.go), and answerAsk indexes nothing at all.
findings.answer: Design D1 and D2 and task T3: an indexer reads the question, every option and the current answer, and every one of the eight writers calls it in its own transaction, passing the targets it returns into the ReferenceChanges of the event it already publishes. Departure 4 records that the answer path is new work.

findings.finding: F2: an ask's own refs rows would double-count once a part holds the same link, because heldByABlock iterates comment and message alone.
findings.answer: Design D2 and task T4: heldByABlock gains an ask arm over ask_block_refs keyed on ask_id, so the ask-level row is hidden wherever a part holds the link, and ?from=<ask> unions the part links. The count of edges for a link in a question is unchanged.

findings.finding: F3: for a block ask the document's own block already indexes the same markdown, so an ask-part source would be a third source for one written link.
findings.answer: Design D2: a part's text is the row's text. A markdown link in a block ask lives in the document block alone, as packages/envoy/AGENTS.md states; a bare dispatch:// URL is in the row and becomes a part link, which keeps the edge count exactly as today.

findings.finding: F4: the row holds a block ask's question and options as plain text, so a markdown link written in the block is not in the row at all.
findings.answer: Design D2, same decision, and the driver's R7 section writes bare dispatch:// URLs rather than markdown links.

findings.finding: F5: the wording revision R1 and A15 need cannot be derived from events — restoreWordings writes with no event, and restoreIssueAsksTx appends an ask.opened for an unchanged wording.
findings.answer: Design D1: ask_block_state.revision, bumped by the indexer when the parts changed, with a trigger on insert or update of question, options, answer. No write path counts, so both event-free and spurious writers are covered; T3 tests restoreWordings explicitly.

findings.finding: F6: a label-hash option id moves whenever a label is rewritten, and two writers rewrite labels with no event, so a pinned reference would 404 where A15 requires 'changed'.
findings.answer: Design D1 and departure 2: ids are minted and stored, carried by itemblocks.Align's five rules, with the part's type salted into the hash matchKey reads.

findings.finding: F7: dispatch://INFRA-721 changes what an option is and is in flight.
findings.answer: The 'Coordination with dispatch://INFRA-721' section: a message to its implementer and the INFRA controller before T3, and the base brought in only at the real conflict. Its own plan adds no wire field, so the part design is unaffected by the order.

findings.finding: F8: the tree's plan says no migration is needed and names no census.
findings.answer: Task T2: two migrations, each with its .census.sql, numbered from main's highest plus one (0146 after sjawhar/legion#2394 takes 0145), with the graph_edges view restated.

findings.finding: F9: which storage kind an ask part uses — the tree's plan says kind block with an ask/ prefix, while refs.TargetOf already computes ask_block.
findings.answer: Design D3 and departure 3: storage kind ask_block, API node kind block, id ask/<uuid>#<part>, with a nodeLoaders entry; T4 step 3 extends TestAnOlderBuildSkipsItemBlockRows to pin it.

findings.finding: F10: a #b- fragment on a document page's ?ask= — the tree's plan resolves it to the part, the code returns the ask.
findings.answer: Design D4 and departure 5: a part is named on the ask's own page only; a document page keeps naming the ask, as ?comment= does. T1 holds both in the shared reference tables.

findings.finding: F11: is an ask part's parent_version null, as the tree's plan says?
findings.answer: Design D1 and task T4: parent_version is the part's changed_revision, as a comment block's is, now that the revision exists. A11's assertion reads it.

findings.finding: F12: which answers are parts — every historical answer or the current one?
findings.answer: Design D1: the current answer is a live part, a replaced one keeps its row as a removed part, and no history before this release is rebuilt (R9's rule). Raised to the architect as question 1, since the tree's plan reads as though every historical answer were a part.

findings.finding: Section C: eight acceptance lines no machine could check as written (A6's 'on that option', A11's 'empty values only where R12 allows', A15's ask clause with no revision to pin to, R7, R10, R11's reply clause, R12 for a removed part, R14).
findings.answer: The 'Acceptance criteria, their surface and their command' table: each line names its surface and a command a tester re-runs, with the exact printed shape for A6, the six facts for A11, the published revision for A15, one-edge-per-link for R7, the 404 text for R10, the three reply cases for R11, the removed part's editor and time for R12, and the pinned kind test for R14.

findings.finding: Section D: thirteen places that assume a block belongs to a document, a comment or a message, the 0142 replies_to view arm among them, plus rebuild-refs, the reconciliation counts and the graph_edges tests.
findings.answer: Tasks T2, T3, T4 and T5 name every one of them by file and symbol: the split view arm, ReplyBlocks' inner join, ItemKind.tables, heldByABlock, itemBlockIDs, repliesToABlockOf, itemRead, blockKindAt, the WholeDocuments source list, Outgoing, CountedChanges, Stamp, parseReferencesQuery's two assigning ifs and both reply refusals including comment_delivery.go's.

findings.finding: Section E: nothing prints a part id, nothing publishes the revision, no surface lists an ask's parts, and the production surface was unnamed.
findings.answer: T4 publishes AskOption.id, AskAnswer.id and Ask.revision; T6 prints each option with its reference in dispatch read; ?to=<ask>&kind=part_of lists the parts, so no blocks route is added (D5); the production check command is in the acceptance table, from this deployment's own instructions.

findings.finding: Section F: thirteen claims of the tree's plan that are false against main — two workflow files that do not exist, CHANGELOG.md edits, refs_block_owner, refs.ToID, hydrateReplyBlocks, and sixteen moved line numbers.
findings.answer: The Constraints section carries the real CI job names from .github/workflows/ci.yaml and the changie fragment convention; departure 6 records the rest; this plan cites symbols, never line numbers.

specDepartures.spec: The tree's plan for PR6: 'An ask's parts need no migration as graph nodes, because they are computed from the ask row and its answer events on every read', and 'Ask parts have no graph_edges arm'.
specDepartures.plan: An ask's parts are stored blocks: four tables (ask_blocks, ask_block_texts, ask_block_state, ask_block_refs), two migrations, a trigger, a seed and a reconciliation arm, mirroring migration 0142's comment family.
specDepartures.evidence: R7 for asks needs a table to hold a part's source rows, as comment_block_refs does; R1 and A15 need a revision counter and the text at each revision, as comment_block_texts holds; and docs/decided_wording.go's restoreWordings rewrites an ask's question and options and appends no event (its own comment says so), so no event replay can serve either.

outcome.scope: this slice adds two migrations and four tables, which the tree's plan said it would not

specDepartures.spec: The tree's plan's contract item 14: an option's part id is o- and the first 8 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its trimmed label, an answer's a- and the hash of its answerer and time, computed on every read and never stored.
specDepartures.plan: Part ids are minted and stored, carried across edits by itemblocks.Align's five rules, with the part's type salted into the hash Align matches on.
specDepartures.evidence: docs/decided_wording.go's restore and docs/ask_blocks.go's settlement write-back both rewrite an option's label with no ask.edited event, so a label hash moves the id and a pinned reference answers 404 where A15 requires it to read 'changed'; itemblocks.matchKey matches on the hash alone, with no type, so an option whose text equalled the question's would take the question's id.

outcome.scope: the ask part id contract changes from a content hash computed on read to a minted id stored with the part

specDepartures.spec: The tree's plan's Task 6.2: 'loadBlockNodes sends ids that begin ask/ to loadAskPartNodes', that is, storage kind block with an ask/ prefix.
specDepartures.plan: The storage kind is ask_block, with a nodeLoaders entry of its own; the API node kind stays block, the id is ask/<uuid>#<part> and loadBlockNodes keeps resolving document blocks alone.
specDepartures.evidence: refs.TargetOf already computes ItemKind(ref.Item).BlockKind() the moment text.parseBlock sets Ref.Item, and refs/item_block_nodes_test.go's TestAnOlderBuildSkipsItemBlockRows pins for comments and messages that no item block row is stored under kind block.

outcome.scope: the storage kind of an ask part, a contract item of the tree's plan

specDepartures.spec: The tree's plan for PR6 lists its writers as the ask read sites and editAsk; it names no indexing on the answer path.
specDepartures.plan: api/ask_transitions.go's answerAsk and resolveAsk index the ask's parts, and their events' references_changed name what moved.
specDepartures.evidence: answerAsk writes `update asks set state = 'answered', answer = $2` and calls nothing in refs today, so an ask.answered moves no edge; with the answer as a part it must.

outcome.scope: the answer and resolve transitions join the writers this slice changes

specDepartures.spec: The tree's plan's Task 6.1 Step 3: '/issues/CORE-1/asks/<uuid>#b-question resolves to the question', and its table rows read a part from a document page's ask fragment.
specDepartures.plan: A #b- fragment names a part on the ask's own page only; on a document page, ?ask=<id>#b-<block> keeps naming the ask.
specDepartures.evidence: text/refs.go's documentPage returns the item and ignores the fragment when ?ask= or ?comment= is set, because the dashboard writes the document block's fragment beside it; the same rule already holds for ?comment=.

acceptance: a dashboard URL of a document page with ?ask= and a #b- fragment resolves to the ask, not to the ask's part
